children: has acquired Inferize, an Israel-based AI startup that specializes in reducing idle GPU capacity and accelerates the deployment of large models, the neocloud announced today.

Inferize's technology reduces what's known as "cold starts," which is the time models need to load before serving requests. Cold starts can leave GPUs idle during a launch as demand spikes and new instances occur. Inferize's technology is intended to reduce this idle time and scale more in unison with usage.
No financial details on the acquisition were provided, but the Calcalist estimated the deal ranged from $100M to $150M.
Nebius plans to add Inferize's experienced engineers to its inference team.

"Running inference well takes more than fast GPUs and optimized models," said Nebius Chief Technology Officer Danila Shtan. "The whole system needs to respond when demand changes, including how quickly additional capacity is ready to serve customers. Inferize brings technology that accelerates that process and a team with deep expertise in GPU systems. We're bringing both into Token Factory to make it more responsive to customer demand and get more useful work out of our infrastructure. The team's contribution will extend well beyond this first integration."

"Keeping spare GPUs running is the price of being ready for demand," added Inferize co-founder and CEO Guy Bortnikov. "Removing that cost is what we built Inferize to do, and Nebius is where it can go straight into the platform."
Bortnikov co-founded Granulate as well, which developed software for optimizing computing infrastructure. That company was acquired by Intel in 2022.
Nebius also recently acquired Eigen AI in a deal valued at $643M and Clarifai (value not disclosed) to improve inference and model optimization.

title: Nebius acquires Inferize to accelerate AI model scale-ups; adds engineers to inference team
